title: Given a Scenario, Use Microsoft Windows Operating System Features and Tools

sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: Windows includes built-in tools for processes, services, startup, hardware, storage, logs, scheduling, certificates, accounts, performance, system configuration, cleanup, drive optimization, and Registry editing.
The main mental model is: problem type → correct Windows tool.
sections.callout: For each scenario, identify exactly what must be inspected or changed, then choose the most direct built-in tool.

sections.title: Maestro Focus
paragraphs: When a Windows troubleshooting or administrative task appears, can you identify the fastest built-in tool for the job?
bullets: Local accounts and groups → Local Users and Groups
Hardware and OS inventory → System Information

sections.title: Task Manager
paragraphs: Task Manager provides a quick view of running applications and processes, system performance, users, startup programs, and services. It is the first stop when the question is what is running or consuming resources right now.

entries.title: Services
paragraphs: The Services area shows Windows services and their current status.
entries.recognitionCue: Inspect a background Windows service quickly → Task Manager Services.

entries.title: Startup
paragraphs: The Startup area manages applications that launch when Windows starts or a user signs in.
entries.recognitionCue: Too many applications slow sign-in or boot → Task Manager Startup.

entries.title: Performance
paragraphs: The Performance area gives an overview of CPU, memory, disk, and network utilization.
entries.recognitionCue: Check CPU or RAM use quickly → Task Manager Performance.

entries.title: Processes
paragraphs: The Processes area shows applications and background processes and lets a technician identify or end an unresponsive or resource-heavy process.
entries.recognitionCue: An application is frozen → Task Manager Processes.

entries.title: Users
paragraphs: The Users area shows logged-in users and their resource usage.
entries.recognitionCue: Determine who is signed in and using resources → Task Manager Users.

sections.title: Microsoft Management Console (MMC) Snap-Ins
paragraphs: Microsoft Management Console provides a common framework for Windows administrative tools called snap-ins. CompTIA expects recognition of the tool name, its job, and its .msc command.
sections.callout: MMC is the container; the snap-in is the task-specific tool.

sections.title: Event Viewer — eventvwr.msc
paragraphs: Event Viewer displays application, security, system, and other Windows event logs. Use it to investigate recorded errors, warnings, and significant events.
sections.callout: What happened? Read the logs in Event Viewer.

sections.title: Disk Management — diskmgmt.msc
paragraphs: Disk Management manages physical disks, partitions, volumes, drive letters, and formatting.
sections.callout: Create or inspect a partition, volume, or drive letter → Disk Management.

sections.title: Task Scheduler — taskschd.msc
paragraphs: Task Scheduler runs actions automatically in response to a time, schedule, trigger, or event.
sections.callout: Run a maintenance script every night → Task Scheduler.

sections.title: Device Manager — devmgmt.msc
paragraphs: Device Manager displays installed hardware and drivers. Use it to identify device problems, update drivers, and disable or enable hardware.
sections.callout: A device shows a warning icon or needs a driver → Device Manager.

sections.title: Certificate Manager — certmgr.msc
paragraphs: Certificate Manager displays and manages digital certificates associated with the current user.
sections.callout: View or manage an installed user certificate → Certificate Manager.

sections.title: Local User and Groups — lusrmgr.msc
paragraphs: Local Users and Groups manages local user accounts, local groups, and group membership.
sections.callout: Add a local account to the Administrators group → Local Users and Groups.

sections.title: Performance Monitor — perfmon.msc
paragraphs: Performance Monitor provides detailed performance counters and supports sustained or historical measurement.
sections.callout: Track detailed CPU or disk counters over time → Performance Monitor.

sections.title: Group Policy Editor — gpedit.msc
paragraphs: Group Policy Editor configures supported local computer and user policies.
sections.callout: Configure a local Windows policy → Group Policy Editor.

entries.title: System Information — msinfo32.exe
paragraphs: System Information displays detailed hardware, components, OS environment, and system-resource inventory.
entries.memoryHook: What is inside this PC? → msinfo32.
entries.recognitionCue: Find the system model, BIOS version, RAM, and OS inventory → System Information.

entries.title: Resource Monitor — resmon.exe
paragraphs: Resource Monitor shows detailed real-time CPU, memory, disk, and network activity by process.
entries.memoryHook: Who is using resources right now? → resmon.
entries.recognitionCue: Identify the process generating current network traffic → Resource Monitor.

entries.title: System Configuration — msconfig.exe
paragraphs: System Configuration helps isolate and troubleshoot startup, boot, and service configuration problems.
entries.recognitionCue: Troubleshoot broader Windows startup behavior → System Configuration.

entries.title: Disk Cleanup — cleanmgr.exe
paragraphs: Disk Cleanup removes temporary, cached, and other unnecessary files to recover storage space.
entries.recognitionCue: Remove unneeded temporary files → Disk Cleanup.

entries.title: Disk Defragment — dfrgui.exe
paragraphs: The drive optimization interface traditionally defragments hard disks. Windows handles SSD optimization differently, so do not treat SSDs like mechanical HDDs.
entries.recognitionCue: A traditional hard drive is heavily fragmented → Disk Defragment.

entries.title: Registry Editor — regedit.exe
paragraphs: Registry Editor views and changes the Windows Registry, a low-level configuration database for Windows, users, applications, and hardware. Incorrect changes can seriously affect the system.
entries.recognitionCue: Inspect or change a specific Registry key → Registry Editor.

sections.title: Task Manager, Resource Monitor, and Performance Monitor

table.caption: Choose the right monitoring tool
rows: Detailed current CPU, memory, disk, and network use

sections.callout: Task Manager is quick; Resource Monitor is detailed and live; Performance Monitor measures counters over time.

entries.title: Event Viewer vs. Performance Monitor
paragraphs: Event Viewer answers what logged event occurred. Performance Monitor answers how performance counters behave.

entries.title: Disk Management vs. Disk Cleanup vs. Disk Defragment
paragraphs: Disk Management changes storage structure; Disk Cleanup frees space; Disk Defragment optimizes fragmented HDD data layout.

entries.title: Device Manager vs. System Information
paragraphs: Device Manager configures and troubleshoots hardware and drivers. System Information reads detailed system inventory.

entries.title: Task Manager Startup vs. System Configuration
paragraphs: Task Manager Startup controls startup applications. msconfig supports broader startup, boot, and service troubleshooting.

entries.title: Registry Editor vs. Group Policy Editor
paragraphs: regedit directly edits Registry data. gpedit configures supported administrative policies.

sections.title: Recognition Cues
bullets: Kill a frozen process → Task Manager
Manage startup applications → Task Manager Startup
Manage partitions and volumes → Disk Management
Schedule an automatic action → Task Scheduler
Driver or device problem → Device Manager
Manage local users and groups → lusrmgr.msc
Hardware and OS inventory → System Information
Optimize a fragmented HDD → Disk Defragment

sections.title: Objective 1.4 Exam Trap
paragraphs: Several Windows tools may sound plausible. Focus on the exact object being inspected or changed: process, event log, performance counter, device, inventory, partition, free space, startup item, policy, or Registry key.

entries.title: Current Activity vs. Historical Events
paragraphs: Task Manager and Resource Monitor show current activity. Event Viewer shows recorded events.

entries.title: Live Detail vs. Counter Tracking
paragraphs: Resource Monitor provides detailed live use; Performance Monitor measures counters and trends.

entries.title: Storage Structure vs. Storage Space
paragraphs: Disk Management handles partitions and volumes; Disk Cleanup removes unnecessary files.

entries.title: Hardware Management vs. Inventory
paragraphs: Device Manager changes or troubleshoots devices and drivers; msinfo32 reports system information.

entries.title: Policy vs. Registry
paragraphs: gpedit configures policy; regedit directly edits Registry keys and values.

bullets: Current resource overview → Task Manager Performance
